newsitem.title: USA: Haiti presidential guard linked to murders - paper.
newsitem.headline: Haiti presidential guard linked to murders - paper.

text.p: Members of Haiti's U.S.-trained presidential security unit have been linked to last month's assassinations of two right-wing opposition politicians, the Miami Herald reported on Saturday.

U.S. officials have pressed President Rene Preval to take action against those involved, the newspaper said. Preval was not believed to have any involvement in the August 20 killings, according to unidentified U.S. sources quoted by the newspaper.

Antoine Leroy, a senior member of the conservative Mobilisation for National Development Party, and Jacques Dorval, another party member, were killed a day after drive-by attacks on the Parliament building and the Port-au-Prince police headquarters.
At the time, the attacks were blamed on former members of Haiti's once-feared army.

The presidential security unit consists of about 100 guards who are responsible for the security of President Preval and former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide. Many of the guards were with Aristide when he was in exile following a 1991 military coup.
The U.S. State Department's diplomatic security unit helped train the guards.
"The allegation is that this was a counter-effort by the (presidential) security unit," a White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told the Herald.

A U.S. congressional source told the Herald that evidence linking the security unit to the killings included eyewitness accounts provided to the U.S. embassy, telephone intercepts and recovered shell casings.

U.S. officials and other western diplomats are concerned at the growing level of violence in Haiti in recent weeks, which comes as the U.S. presidential campaign enters its final phase. President Clinton has said that the U.S.-led military intervention to restore democracy in Haiti in 1994 was one of his most important foreign policy successes.
